She stands left of the open doorway, her body angled toward the passage but her face still visible in a gentle three-quarter view. Her front foot rests just before the brass threshold and her weight remains on the rear foot. Her left hand holds a closed ivory-colored folding fan at waist height; her right hand falls naturally beside the blue silk skirt. The usher stands to the right of the passage, his left hand around the door handle and his right palm extended low toward the empty route through the door. They look toward each other. Her slightly parted lips and attentive gaze carry a private breath of anticipation within a public ceremony. A pale blue silk court gown has a fitted square-neck bodice, elbow-length lace cuffs and a broad structured skirt whose folds catch the window light. The usher wears an embroidered dark coat and knee breeches. Two waiting courtiers in restrained silk court dress remain several paces back, their bodies turned toward the same doorway. The antechamber has pale paneled walls, gilt pilasters and a parquet floor; beyond the open leaf, a deeper red-walled room and a raised empty chair are visible in alignment. Compose a full-length vertical photograph, slightly off the passage axis, with her face and the usher's open palm clear and the threshold entirely visible. Cool afternoon window light shapes her face and the blue silk against the warmer inner room. Use realistic skin texture, tactile silk, controlled gilded highlights and enough depth of field for the social spacing and doorway to read together. The visual center is the interval between her paused step and the usher's permission, with her quiet presence carrying the portrait's subtle attraction.
